newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arab Potash Company 7-month profits up.
newsitem.headline: Arab Potash Company 7-month profits up.

text.p: Arab Potash Company, stimulated by fast growing Asian demand and improved prices, posted a 27.5 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 23 million dinars in the first seven months of 1996, its general manager said on Thursday.

"Our improved results are due to both a slight improvement in potash prices and a higher overall marketing performance," Suleiman al-Hawari, general manager of Arab Potash Company, the country's only producer, told Reuters.

Company officials expect Arab Potash's profits in 1996 to remain near last year's record pre-tax profit level of 42 million dinars due to higher production costs after the government hiked energy costs this year.
Arab Potash's posted record $182 million dinar sales in 1995, a 35 percent rise on the year before, boosted by increased demand in Asia.
Jordan, one of the world's major producers of potash, a key ingredient in the fertiliser industry, is expected to benefit from the continued growth of its traditional Asian markets.
The company, a key public shareholding company, is 57 percent state-owned but several Arab states, including Saudi Arabia and Kuwait have minority holdings.

India was the leading importer in the first half of 1996 with 192,800 tonnes followed by 87,250 tonnes to Indonesia, 72,950 tonnes to Malaysia and 66,150 000 tonnes to Korea and 66,185 tonnes to Italy.
Potash production rose a slight 2 percent to 805,276 tonnes in the first half 1996 from 787,633 tonnes in the same period last year.
Jordan's potash production rose 15 percent to 1,780,000 tonnes in 1995 after a new $125 million plant that came on stream added 400,000 tonnes to the previous plant capacity of 1.4 million tonnes.
Total sales were steady in the first half of 1996 at 736,075 tonnes from 737,234 tonnes in the same period last year.
